description: DSPy: The framework for programming—not prompting—language models

latest_release.body:
# DSPy 3.4.1

DSPy 3.4.1 makes GEPA's structured `InstructionProposer` the default instruction proposer and lets `dspy.RLM` build DSPy sub-agents from inside its REPL. It also adds Python 3.15 support, fixes a 3.4.0 import crash, and includes streaming, adapter, and interpreter fixes.

```bash
pip install --upgrade "dspy==3.4.1"
```

**Upgrade notices.** GEPA's default reflection request changes shape, so optimization results can differ from 3.4.0 even with the same seed. The reflection LM must now be a `dspy.LM` that can return JSON. Every RLM prompt now includes a sub-agent section, and `max_llm_calls` now also counts sub-agent LM calls. `dspy.ReActV2` signatures can no longer declare inputs named `history` or `tools`. Programs saved on 3.4.0 with a null `Score` level no longer load. See [API and Compatibility Changes](#api-and-compatibility-changes).

The [3.5 LM-interface cutoff](https://dspy.ai/community/normalized-lm-api-migration/#the-35-cutoff) announced in 3.4.0 still applies. Legacy `forward()`/`aforward()` custom LMs, the legacy-engine wrappers, custom `complete_legacy()` shortcuts, and OpenAI-style `messages=` calls are deprecated and will be removed in 3.5. `lm("hello")` stays supported.

## Highlights

### `InstructionProposer` Is GEPA's Default Proposer — @dbreunig

`dspy.GEPA` now builds `InstructionProposer()` when you don't pass `instruction_proposer=`. The old default formatted reflective examples into one raw prompt and pulled the new instruction out of backticks. The new one calls the reflection LM through `dspy.Predict` with a `JSONAdapter`. Reflective examples stay structured, so `dspy.History` inputs, tool trajectories, and `dspy.Type` values such as `dspy.Image` (including nested images) reach the reflection LM as structured content instead of text placeholders. GEPA's reflection instructions are unchanged.

You can configure the proposer directly:

```python
import dspy
from dspy.teleprompt.gepa import InstructionProposer

optimizer = dspy.GEPA(
    metric=metric,
    reflection_lm=dspy.LM("openai/gpt-5"),
    instruction_proposer=InstructionProposer(
        skills=["./skills/prompt-engineering"],
        additional_instructions="Write instructions in imperative voice.",
        max_chars=1500,
        truncate_history_outputs=True,
    ),
    auto="medium",
)
```

- `skills`: reference material for the reflection LM. Pass a path, a directory containing `SKILL.md`, an inline string, or a list of these. YAML frontmatter is parsed at construction.
- `additional_instructions`: extra guidance applied to every proposal.
- `base_instructions`: replaces the reflection prompt but keeps its input and output fields.
- `max_chars`: a hard character limit. A draft that is too long gets one compression attempt; DSPy never truncates an instruction.
- `truncate_history_outputs`: shortens long tool and REPL outputs inside history inputs before rendering, without changing the originals.
- `adapter`: the adapter used for proposal calls. The default is `JSONAdapter()`.

Custom `instruction_proposer` functions receive the same reflective dataset as before, and `MultiModalInstructionProposer` remains available.

This release also fixes reflection inputs that contain a value pydantic can't serialize, such as a `numpy.int64` from a pandas row. That value now renders as `str(value)` in place, instead of turning every example into a Python repr.

PRs: [#10555](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10555); follow-up fix [#10634](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10634) by @isaacbmiller

### RLM Can Build DSPy Sub-Agents — @michaelisaac-dev

Code that `dspy.RLM` writes can now `import dspy` and build sub-agents for subtasks that need structured inputs and outputs, tools, or their own recursion:

- `dspy.Predict` and `dspy.ChainOfThought`
- `dspy.ReActV2`, using the tools you gave the RLM
- a nested `dspy.RLM`, which runs on the same interpreter backend as its pa

detail.readme_excerpt: ## DSPy: _Programming_—not prompting—Foundation Models **Documentation:** [DSPy Docs](https://dspy.ai/) [![PyPI Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/dspy?period=monthly)](https://pepy.tech/projects/dspy) ---- DSPy is the framework for _programming—rather than prompting—language models_. It allows you to iterate fast on **building modular AI systems** and offers algorithms for **optimizing their prompts and weights**, whether you're building simple classifiers, sophisticated RAG pipelines, or Agent loops. DSPy stands for Declarative Self-improving Python. Instead of brittle prompts, you write compositional _Python code_ and use DSPy to **teach your LM to deliver high-quality outputs**. Learn more via our [official documentation site](https://dspy.ai/) or meet the community, seek help, or start contributing via this GitHub repo and our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/XCGy2WDCQB). ## Documentation: [dspy.ai](https://dspy.ai) **Please go to the [DSPy Docs at dspy.ai](https://dspy.ai)** ## Installation ```bash pip install dspy ``` To install the very latest from `main`: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy.git ``` The current LM integration uses bundled native lm15 engines, without a LiteLLM runtime dependency or fallback. See the [LM migration guide](docs/docs/community/normalized-lm-api-migration.md) for breaking changes to provider options, custom LMs, text completions, and embeddings. ## 📜 Citation & Reading More If you're looking to understand the framework, please go to the [DSPy Docs at dspy.ai](https://dspy.ai). If you're looking to understand the underlying research, this is a set of our papers: **[Jul'25] [GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457)** **[Jun'24] [Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11695)** **[Oct'23] [DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03714)** [Jul'24] [Fine-Tuning and Prompt Optimization: Two Great Steps that Work Better Together](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10930) [Jun'24] [Prompts as Auto-Optimized Training Hyperparameters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11706) [Feb'24] [Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14207) [Jan'24] [In-Context Learning for Extreme Multi-Label Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12178) [Dec'23] [DSPy Assertions: Computational Constraints for Self-Refining Language Model Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13382) [Dec'22] [Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval & Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14024.pdf) To stay up to date or lea
